anzsic_codes.name: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction

merger_description:
STRABAG Australia Pty Ltd (**STRABAG Australia**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued shares in KEE Surfacing Pty Ltd (**KEE Surfacing**). To facilitate this share sale, KEE Surfacing will acquire the asphalt-producing and paving assets of Spiers Holdings Australia Pty Ltd (**Spiers**) used to conduct KEE Surfacing’s road surfacing business (the share sale and the asset sale together, the **Acquisition**).

STRABAG Australia is a wholly-owned subsidiary of STRABAG SE, a European construction group listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange (together with its related bodies corporate, the**STRABAG Group**).

STRABAG Australia’s business is primarily to act as the holding company of Georgiou Group Pty Ltd (**Georgiou**), and to perform works when its overseas arms conduct business in Australia. Georgiou supplies building and infrastructure construction services across Australia in respect of major transport projects, commercial buildings, urban land development, defence projects, and resource engineering for both government and private clients.

KEE Surfacing provides road surfacing services (for the purposes of road construction and maintenance) to customers in Western Australia and, to a limited extent, the Northern Territory. KEE Surfacing’s customers include businesses that operate across the road construction and maintenance value chain, including construction businesses and government clients.

Spiers and KEE Surfacing Pty Ltd are separate entities under common ownership within the KEE Group. Spiers Holdings serves as the KEE Group’s dedicated asset holding entity and owns various items of plant and equipment used across the group’s operations. Certain assets utilised in KEE Surfacing’s road surfacing business are owned by Spiers and provided for its use under internal commercial arrangements. To facilitate the transaction, Spiers has entered into an agreement to sell the relevant assets to STRABAG Australia so that the assets required for the ongoing operation of the business transfer as part of the Acquisition.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between STRABAG (and its
connected entities) and KEE Surfacing in the supply of road
surfacing services in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of both civil infrastructure and
building construction services and road surfacing services in
Australia
c. there is low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
